content: Nitazoxanide is prescribed to treat diarrhea in both children and adults caused by the protozoa Cryptosporidium or Giardia. Protozoa are suspected as the cause when diarrhea persists for more than seven days. Nitazoxanide belongs to a class of medications known as antiprotozoal agents. It works by inhibiting the growth of specific protozoa responsible for causing diarrhea. Nitazoxanide is available in tablet form and as a liquid suspension for oral use. It is typically taken with food every 12 hours for three days. It is important to take nitazoxanide at the same times each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take nitazoxanide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If you are using the suspension, shake it well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking nitazoxanide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nitazoxanide or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention anticoagulants (blood thinners) such as warfarin (Coumadin). Your doctor may need to adjust the doses of your medications or monitor you closely for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had HIV, immune system disorders, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking nitazoxanide, contact your doctor immediately. To prevent dehydration caused by diarrhea, ensure that you or your child consumes adequate fluids. Take small, frequent sips of water, fruit juice, sports drinks, or broth. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Nitazoxanide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: stomach pain, headache, upset stomach, vomiting, or discolored urine. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience a skin rash or itching. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Discard any medication that is outdated or no longer needed. Dispose of any unused nitazoxanide suspension after seven days. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Note that each teaspoon of nitazoxanide suspension contains 48 grams of sucrose. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If diarrhea persists after completing the nitazoxanide course, contact your doctor.
